New machine. Its objects are: vesoso, mekukil, kanago, denasa, gumusu, vinatir.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

There are 15 possible nexiom pairs and 2 possible rules, so 30 possibilities in total. Five yes/no tests give at most 32 outcomes, so every test needs to split the remaining possibilities about in half.

Testing 3 of the 6 objects does that:
- **Lights up:** either it is a "needs one" machine with at least one nexiom among the three (12 cases), or a "needs two" machine with both nexioms among the three (3 cases). That is 15 cases.
- **Stays dark:** the other 15 cases.

TEST: vesoso, mekukil, kanago
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The first test stayed dark, so 15 cases remain:
- **Needs one:** both nexioms must be among denasa, gumusu and vinatir. That is 3 pairs.
- **Needs two:** any pair not entirely inside vesoso, mekukil and kanago. That is 12 pairs.

Testing vesoso, mekukil, denasa and gumusu splits these almost evenly:
- **Lights up (8 cases):**
  - Needs one: denasa+gumusu, denasa+vinatir or gumusu+vinatir.
  - Needs two: vesoso+denasa, vesoso+gumusu, mekukil+denasa, mekukil+gumusu or denasa+gumusu.
- **Stays dark (7 cases):** all are "needs two" machines. The pair is kanago+denasa, kanago+gumusu, kanago+vinatir, vesoso+vinatir, mekukil+vinatir, denasa+vinatir or gumusu+vinatir.

Either branch leaves at most 8 cases, which 3 more yes/no tests can tell apart.

TEST: vesoso, mekukil, denasa, gumusu
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Eight cases remain after the second test lit up:
- **Needs one:** denasa+gumusu, denasa+vinatir or gumusu+vinatir.
- **Needs two:** vesoso+denasa, vesoso+gumusu, mekukil+denasa, mekukil+gumusu or denasa+gumusu.

Testing vesoso, mekukil and denasa splits these exactly in half:
- **Lights up (4 cases):** needs one with denasa+gumusu or denasa+vinatir, or needs two with vesoso+denasa or mekukil+denasa.
- **Stays dark (4 cases):** needs one with gumusu+vinatir, or needs two with vesoso+gumusu, mekukil+gumusu or denasa+gumusu.

Two more tests can then tell apart the 4 cases in either branch.

TEST: vesoso, mekukil, denasa
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Four cases remain after the third test lit up:
- **Needs one:** denasa+gumusu or denasa+vinatir.
- **Needs two:** vesoso+denasa or mekukil+denasa.

Denasa is a nexiom in every case. So testing denasa alone splits them exactly in half:
- **Lights up:** it is a "needs one" machine. Testing gumusu next will show whether the pair is denasa+gumusu or denasa+vinatir.
- **Stays dark:** it is a "needs two" machine. Testing vesoso with denasa next will show whether the pair is vesoso+denasa or mekukil+denasa.

TEST: denasa
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Denasa alone lit the machine, so this is a "needs one" machine. The second nexiom is either gumusu or vinatir.

Testing gumusu alone settles it:
- **Lights up:** the nexioms are denasa and gumusu.
- **Stays dark:** the nexioms are denasa and vinatir.

TEST: gumusu
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Gumusu alone lit the machine, so gumusu is the second nexiom. The fourth test, with denasa alone, had already shown the machine needs only one nexiom.

All five results agree with this:
- **Test 1 (vesoso, mekukil, kanago) stayed dark:** neither nexiom was on it.
- **Test 2 (vesoso, mekukil, denasa, gumusu) lit up:** denasa and gumusu were both on it.
- **Test 3 (vesoso, mekukil, denasa) lit up:** denasa was on it.
- **Test 4 (denasa) lit up:** denasa was on it.
- **Test 5 (gumusu) lit up:** gumusu was on it.

ANSWER: nexioms = denasa, gumusu; needs = one

New machine. Its objects are: muvafi, bukuvis, digamok, kakubur, gukamor, vamenil.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing three of the six objects. Every possible answer (15 pairs × 2 modes = 30) splits evenly here: 15 would light and 15 would not.

TEST: muvafi, bukuvis, digamok
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

After the first test, 15 possibilities remain. In "needs one" mode, both nexioms must be among kakubur, gukamor and vamenil, which gives 3 pairs. In "needs two" mode, any pair works except one entirely within muvafi, bukuvis and digamok, which gives 12 pairs.

Testing muvafi, bukuvis, kakubur and gukamor splits these about evenly.
- **Would light (8):** all 3 "needs one" pairs, plus 5 "needs two" pairs: MK, MG, BK, BG, KG.
- **Would not light (7):** the "needs two" pairs involving vamenil or digamok: MV, BV, DV, KV, GV, DK, DG.

TEST: muvafi, bukuvis, kakubur, gukamor
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Eight possibilities remain:
- **Needs one (3):** kakubur+gukamor, kakubur+vamenil, gukamor+vamenil.
- **Needs two (5):** muvafi+kakubur, muvafi+gukamor, bukuvis+kakubur, bukuvis+gukamor, kakubur+gukamor.

With 3 tests left, each test must split the remaining possibilities exactly in half. Testing muvafi, bukuvis and kakubur does that:
- **Would light (4):** kakubur+gukamor (one), kakubur+vamenil (one), muvafi+kakubur (two), bukuvis+kakubur (two).
- **Would not light (4):** gukamor+vamenil (one), muvafi+gukamor (two), bukuvis+gukamor (two), kakubur+gukamor (two).

TEST: muvafi, bukuvis, kakubur
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Four possibilities remain:
- **Needs one:** kakubur+gukamor, kakubur+vamenil.
- **Needs two:** muvafi+kakubur, bukuvis+kakubur.

Testing kakubur alone splits these in half:
- **Lights up:** it needs one nexiom (kakubur+gukamor or kakubur+vamenil).
- **Stays dark:** it needs two (muvafi+kakubur or bukuvis+kakubur).

My last test can then settle which of the two pairs it is.

TEST: kakubur
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Kakubur alone lit the machine, so it needs only one nexiom and kakubur is a nexiom. The other nexiom is either gukamor or vamenil. Testing gukamor alone will tell: if it lights, gukamor is the second nexiom; if not, vamenil is.

TEST: gukamor
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Gukamor lit the machine on its own, so it is the second nexiom. This fits every earlier result:
- **Test 1 (dark):** muvafi, bukuvis and digamok contained neither nexiom.
- **Tests 2 and 3 (lit):** both included kakubur, which is enough on its own.
- **Tests 4 and 5 (lit):** kakubur alone and gukamor alone each lit it, so this machine needs only one nexiom.

ANSWER: nexioms = kakubur, gukamor; needs = one

New machine. Its objects are: mubupul, limurus, fokipen, sukoren, nifugi, meposik.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half the objects. This splits the 30 possibilities (15 pairs × 2 rules) evenly: 15 would make it light and 15 would not.

TEST: mubupul, limurus, fokipen
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Since the machine stayed dark, there are 15 possibilities left:
- **Needs one:** both nexioms are among sukoren, nifugi, meposik (3 pairs).
- **Needs two:** any pair except those entirely within mubupul, limurus, fokipen (12 pairs).

This next test splits them 8 / 7:
- **It lights if:** the rule is "needs one" (any of the 3 pairs), or the rule is "needs two" and the pair is sukoren-nifugi, mubupul-sukoren, mubupul-nifugi, limurus-sukoren or limurus-nifugi. That is 8 possibilities.
- **It stays dark for:** the other 7 "needs two" pairs.

TEST: mubupul, limurus, sukoren, nifugi
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

There are 8 possibilities left after two tests:
- **Needs one:** the pair is sukoren-nifugi, sukoren-meposik or nifugi-meposik.
- **Needs two:** the pair is sukoren-nifugi, mubupul-sukoren, mubupul-nifugi, limurus-sukoren or limurus-nifugi.

This test splits them 4 / 4:
- **It lights for:** "needs one" with sukoren-nifugi or sukoren-meposik, or "needs two" with mubupul-sukoren or limurus-sukoren.
- **It stays dark for:** "needs one" with nifugi-meposik, or "needs two" with sukoren-nifugi, mubupul-nifugi or limurus-nifugi.

Each half of 4 can then be split 2 / 2 and then 1 / 1, so the last two tests will settle it.

TEST: sukoren, mubupul, limurus
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Four possibilities remain after three tests:
- **Needs one:** the pair is sukoren-nifugi or sukoren-meposik.
- **Needs two:** the pair is mubupul-sukoren or limurus-sukoren.

Sukoren is a nexiom in every case, so testing it alone splits them 2 / 2:
- **If it lights:** the rule is "needs one". I'll then test nifugi to tell sukoren-nifugi from sukoren-meposik.
- **If it stays dark:** the rule is "needs two". I'll then test sukoren with mubupul to tell mubupul-sukoren from limurus-sukoren.

TEST: sukoren
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Sukoren lit up by itself, so this machine **needs one** nexiom. Only two pairs fit all the results so far: sukoren-nifugi or sukoren-meposik.

Testing nifugi alone settles it:
- **If it lights:** the nexioms are sukoren and nifugi.
- **If it stays dark:** the nexioms are sukoren and meposik.

TEST: nifugi
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Nifugi stayed dark, so it is not a nexiom. With sukoren lighting the machine by itself, the only possibility left is that the nexioms are **sukoren and meposik**, and the machine **needs one**.

This fits every result:
1. **mubupul, limurus, fokipen:** no nexiom, so it stayed dark.
2. **mubupul, limurus, sukoren, nifugi:** sukoren is there, so it lit.
3. **sukoren, mubupul, limurus:** sukoren is there, so it lit.
4. **sukoren alone:** it lit, which shows one nexiom is enough.
5. **nifugi alone:** not a nexiom, so it stayed dark.

ANSWER: nexioms = sukoren, meposik; needs = one

New machine. Its objects are: tegofa, gizapas, rivoda, rasemen, norupen, ditilu.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

Exactly two of the six objects are nexioms. That gives 15 possible pairs. Each pair could go with either rule, so there are 30 possibilities in total. Five yes/no tests give at most 32 outcomes, so each test needs to split the remaining possibilities roughly in half.

I'll test three of the six objects first.
- **Needs one:** the machine lights unless both nexioms are among the other three. That is 12 lit cases and 3 unlit.
- **Needs two:** it lights only if both nexioms are among these three. That is 3 lit cases and 12 unlit.

Overall that is 15 lit and 15 unlit, an even split.

TEST: tegofa, gizapas, rivoda
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

After the first test, 15 possibilities remain:
- **Needs one:** both nexioms must be among rasemen, norupen and ditilu. That leaves 3 pairs.
- **Needs two:** any pair except one lying entirely within tegofa, gizapas and rivoda. That leaves 12 pairs.

Three tests after this one can only tell apart 8 cases, so this test must leave at most 8 on either side.

Testing rasemen, norupen, tegofa and gizapas:
- **Needs one:** every pair from rasemen, norupen and ditilu includes rasemen or norupen, so all 3 light up.
- **Needs two:** it lights for pairs drawn from these four objects, except tegofa with gizapas (already ruled out). That is 5 lit cases.

That gives 8 lit and 7 unlit, an even enough split.

TEST: rasemen, norupen, tegofa, gizapas
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Eight possibilities remain after two tests:
- **Needs one:** the pair is one of {rasemen, norupen}, {rasemen, ditilu} or {norupen, ditilu}.
- **Needs two:** the pair is one of {rasemen, norupen}, {rasemen, tegofa}, {rasemen, gizapas}, {norupen, tegofa} or {norupen, gizapas}.

With two tests left after this one I can separate 4 cases, so this test must split the 8 into 4 and 4.

Testing rasemen, tegofa and ditilu:
- **Lights (4 cases):** all three "needs one" pairs, since each contains rasemen or ditilu. Also "needs two" with {rasemen, tegofa}.
- **Stays dark (4 cases):** "needs two" with {rasemen, norupen}, {rasemen, gizapas}, {norupen, tegofa} or {norupen, gizapas}.

TEST: rasemen, tegofa, ditilu
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Four possibilities remain after three tests:
- **Needs one:** the pair is {rasemen, norupen}, {rasemen, ditilu} or {norupen, ditilu}.
- **Needs two:** the pair is {rasemen, tegofa}.

This test must split these 2 and 2 so the last test can settle it. Testing rasemen alone does that:
- **Lights:** the pair is "needs one" with {rasemen, norupen} or {rasemen, ditilu}.
- **Stays dark:** the pair is "needs one" with {norupen, ditilu}, or "needs two" with {rasemen, tegofa}.

In either case, testing norupen alone next will separate the last two.

TEST: rasemen
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Two possibilities remain after four tests:
- **Needs one:** the pair is {norupen, ditilu}.
- **Needs two:** the pair is {rasemen, tegofa}.

Testing norupen alone separates them:
- **Lights:** the machine needs one nexiom, and the pair is {norupen, ditilu}. Under the other possibility a single object can't light it.
- **Stays dark:** the machine needs two, and the pair is {rasemen, tegofa}.

TEST: norupen
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Norupen lit up on its own, so the machine needs only one nexiom, and the nexioms are norupen and ditilu.

This fits every test:
- **Test 1 (tegofa, gizapas, rivoda):** no nexiom was present, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 2 (rasemen, norupen, tegofa, gizapas):** norupen was present, so it lit.
- **Test 3 (rasemen, tegofa, ditilu):** ditilu was present, so it lit.
- **Test 4 (rasemen):** rasemen is not a nexiom, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 5 (norupen):** norupen is a nexiom, so it lit.

ANSWER: nexioms = norupen, ditilu; needs = one
